title: Project sessions can open fresh sessions themselves

requirements.text: In the app, genlock open from a project session (no Assistant env) writes an open request for its own project, on --user-said or --relayed
From a project session, genlock open naming another project, or with no yes, is refused and writes nothing
The app opens a fresh session for open requests from any project session, in that session's own project only
requirements.check: file: app/Sources/GenlockApp/AppModel.swift openSessionsIfAsked; swift build passes

requirements.text: Outside the app, genlock open starts a new terminal session on the prompt (or prints the command)
swap --carry-on writes a fresh-session prompt that says to begin at once, without the line asking the user whether to begin
Project-session instructions say how to hand unfinished work to a fresh session when the user is away

text: Diagnosed from nightmaremode transcript 8231cbf5: genlock open is Assistant-only (no path for project sessions); swap's fresh-session prompt ends with 'ask the user whether to begin', which stalls unattended. Blocked on claims held by live session 84a3d710 (T-ZKA3Z, T-FXT7X); asked it to release.

A session handing its work to a fresh one to save tokens needs no yes (swap, and open --handoff which closes this session, keep the session count flat). The only limit is session sprawl: an open that adds a session is capped per project.
user_said: i dont want them to require a 'yes' from me if the goal of the new session is saving tokens. the only reason to limit spinning off a new session is if we're building up dozens of sessions consuming more and more tokens

evidence: superseded by TJ's decision: no yes for token-saving handoffs; replaced by req 7-8
superseded: no yes needed; refusal of other projects moves to req 8

text: In the app, a project session's genlock open --handoff (no yes) writes an open request for its own project and a self-close, so the session count stays flat
A project session's genlock open naming another project is refused, and one that adds a session (no --handoff) is refused once the project has the cap of open sessions
genlock swap goes through with no --user-said
